description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of different models as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)," ranges from 60% to 80%. The plot includes six lines representing different models: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The Base model starts at approximately 65% accuracy at the lowest co-occurrence number and ends around 70% at the highest co-occurrence number. The MEND model begins at around 67% and ends near 75%. The FT model starts at about 65% and ends close to 70%. The MEMIT model begins at approximately 66% and ends around 73%. The IKE model starts at about 64% and ends near 71%. The ROME model begins at around 68% and ends close to 78%. All models show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
